title: BodySys 2025: The 11th Workshop on Body-Centric Computing Systems.
abstract: The 11th Workshop on Body-Centric Computing Systems (BodySys 2025) aims to advance the discussion and innovation around wearable and body-centric technologies for mobile and ubiquitous computing. Building upon a decade of successful workshops, BodySys fosters interdisciplinary dialogue among researchers and practitioners across sensing, communication, AI, health, and human-in-the-loop systems. The 2025 edition will feature keynote talks and ten technical presentations, addressing emerging topics such as implantables, intra-body communication, smart fabrics, and AI-powered wearable computing. The hybrid format encourages broad global participation and positions BodySys as a catalyst for shaping the future of human-centered mobile systems.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Memory-Augmented LLMs for Sustainable Urban Energy Management via Weather-Energy Pattern Learning.
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-memory Large Language Model (LLM) architecture for sustainable urban energy management. Inspired by hippocampal-neocortical interactions, the approach integrates fast learning with long-term memory consolidation to capture weather-energy correlations. The LLM processes meteorological data through natural language interfaces, enabling semantic understanding of weather patterns. Evaluated across European cities using Open-Meteo and ENTSO-E data, the dual-memory LLM achieves 60-85% MAPE improvements over LSTM baselines (2.02-6.13% vs 10.46-17.98%), with cost savings averaging €152M per city. Published version (CC BY 4.0, ACM Open): https://doi.org/10.1145/3714394.3750593 — deposit is a preservation copy with the ACM Digital Library download cover sheet removed. Funding: European Union Horizon Europe programme, Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement No 101073381 (EnTrust — Next-generation of trustworthy agri-data management).

title: Mitigating Interpersonal Variability in Machine Learning Models for Human Behavior Monitoring.
abstract: Machine learning models for human behavior monitoring typically rely on population-level data, assuming that physiological patterns generalize well across individuals. However, this assumption often fails due to interpersonal variability — differences in individuals' physiological responses and subjective interpretations influenced by personal, cultural, and psychological factors. This research first investigates how such variability impacts model performance in two scenarios: sleep monitoring, where label variability arises because individuals assign different subjective ratings to similar physiological patterns, and transport mode recognition, where signal variability occurs as individuals exhibit distinct sensor signals for the same activity. Our empirical findings show that population models struggle to generalize, especially in tasks involving subjective assessments. To overcome these challenges, we firstly propose generative modeling techniques to augment limited user-specific data, and secondly introduce a clustering-based strategy that enables scalable personalization by grouping users according to both physiological signal patterns and labeling behavior.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Toward a Testbed for the Internet of Underwater Things: Challenges and Considerations.
abstract: The Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) is an emerging approach composed of a network of underwater devices, such as sensors, vehicles, and communication nodes, that collaboratively collect, transmit, and analyze data for applications such as ocean monitoring, underwater exploration, and defense. The vision of IoUT includes significant challenges for communication due to signal attenuation, multipath interference, and limited bandwidth. This paper presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a basic underwater acoustic communication system. One of the purposes of this paper was to explore how components coming from the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem can be integrated into the IoUT paradigm. Therefore, we compare a microcontroller with a signal generator for the signal generation process to evaluate performance trade-offs. Performance was assessed across configurations in a pool environment. Key findings include reliable communication at 300 bps up to 6 meters (BER <10% with Hamming encoding) and reliable performance up to 1000 bps at 1 meter (BER ≈ 1%) using a microcontroller instead of a signal generator. This paper demonstrates the first steps to build a testbed to evaluate IoUT solutions that will offer practical insights into the challenges and performance factors of simple underwater acoustic communication.

title: Optimized Personnel Tracking via Theoretical-Actual Acoustic Matching and Joint Active-Passive Constraint.
abstract: Indoor personnel tracking plays a vital role in smart home applications such as security monitoring, elderly care, and appliance control. While passive acoustic localization offers privacy-preserving and non-invasive tracking by estimating the angle-of-arrival (AoA) of sound, it struggles in complex environments with low signal-to-noise ratios and multiple sound sources. Active acoustic methods improve robustness but often suffer from limited deployment flexibility and high computational cost. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel acoustic signal fusion solution via utilizing audio system microphones, fully integrating active and passive acoustic signals. Our approach corrects angular prediction biases in passive sensing and incorporates beamforming-based ranging for accurate distance estimation. By comparing theoretical sampling matrices with real-time data and applying conjugate multiplication, we jointly optimize angle and range measurements. A fusion model further enhances overall tracking accuracy. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method achieves a tracking range of 5.2~m, reduces the median position error to under 11~cm, and improves angular accuracy compared to both passive-only and active-only baselines.

title: Harnessing Unstable Underground Wind for Passive LoRa-Based Human Activity Detection in Coal Mines.
abstract: Human activity detection in underground coal mines is challenged by harsh environments and limited energy availability. This study presents a passive sensing system that harnesses unstable underground wind, induced by mine ventilation, to power LoRa-based communication nodes without relying on external power supplies. To mitigate signal intermittency caused by fluctuating wind energy, a Mean Intermittent Amplitude Ratio (MIAR) algorithm is proposed for extracting robust activity features under high interference. The system incorporates adaptive filtering and sliding window techniques to isolate valid signal segments, enabling reliable personnel detection and gesture recognition. Experimental results show that the Random Forest model achieves robust detection performance, while the ResNet model accurately classifies four representative gestures. The solution demonstrates high deployment flexibility, strong resilience to interference, and full energy autonomy, offering a viable approach for non-contact, battery-free sensing in blind zones and disaster-prone areas of underground coal mines.

title: WiFi-Based People Counting Using Beam-Steerable Antennas: A Test-bed Study.
abstract: RF sensing is an emerging technology paradigm that repurposes existing wireless communication networks, such as WiFi, for imaging and computer vision applications, namely ambient and human sensing. Recent research has demonstrated that RF holography techniques can surpass human vision capabilities in several tasks such as identifying and resolving individuals within dense crowds, interpreting gestures and emotions, and capturing images through walls. The paper explores the use of pattern-reconfigurable antenna devices with unmodified WiFi signals for indoor people discrimination, namely counting the number of people co-present in the space. We discuss signal modeling, integration of beam-steering technology, and adaptation for this purpose. Initial case studies and performance analyses within a test-house environment are also presented.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: DiversityOne Open Challenge: Exploring People's Everyday Life Behavior with Mobile Data.
abstract: Combining passive smartphone sensor data with self-reports enables the study of everyday life behavior. The DiversityOne dataset, recently released to the UbiComp community, overcomes the limitation of existing datasets by containing data from eight countries from both Global South and Global North, including data from 782 college students, combining the data from 26 smartphone sensors and 350K+ self-reports, and extensive demographic and psychosocial survey data from 18K college students. The richness of the dataset opens the way to investigating important problems in multiple disciplines. Existing studies that leverage the dataset have only scratched the surface of the potential research questions it can help answer. Thus, we are organizing this workshop to foster creative and multidisciplinary works on this dataset: from AI and ubiquitous and mobile computing to computational social science and design.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Design and Challenges of Mental Health Assessment Tools Based on Natural Language Interaction.
abstract: Mental health assessments are of central importance to individuals' well-being. Conventional assessment methodologies predominantly depend on clinical interviews and standardised self-report questionnaires. Nevertheless, the efficacy of these methodologies is frequently impeded by factors such as subjectivity, recall bias, and accessibility issues. Furthermore, concerns regarding bias and privacy may result in misreporting in data collected through self-reporting in mental health research. The present study examined the design opportunities and challenges inherent in the development of a mental health assessment tool based on natural language interaction with large language models (LLMs). An interactive prototype system was developed using conversational AI for non-invasive mental health assessment, and was evaluated through semi-structured interviews with 11 mental health professionals (six counsellors and five psychiatrists). The analysis identified key design considerations for future development, highlighting how AI-driven adaptive questioning could potentially enhance the reliability of self-reported data while identifying critical challenges, including privacy protection, algorithmic bias, and cross-cultural applicability. This study provides an empirical foundation for mental health technology innovation by demonstrating the potential and limitations of natural language interaction in mental health assessment.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: FLUX Mouse: A Seamless High-DOF Input Device for Intuitive 3D Interaction.
abstract: Spatial controllers enable rich 3D interactions but often compromise the precision and ergonomic familiarity of traditional mice. Existing solutions typically remain specialized, forcing users to juggle multiple devices or adapt to unfamiliar form factors. We introduce the FLUX Mouse, a spatial input device that combines traditional mouse ergonomics with 3D interaction capabilities, featuring fully automatic transitions between 2D cursor control and 6 DOF spatial interaction. The FLUX Mouse integrates an optical sensor for 2D tasks with an inertial measurement unit and binocular infrared vision tracking for 3D tracking, and uses adaptive pressure sensing to balance precision and speed. Preliminary user feedback suggests intuitive usability, a manageable learning curve, and positive acceptance, indicating the potential to support psychological needs as outlined by Self-Determination Theory across diverse applications from professional modeling to immersive gaming.

title: Read-Range Extension with Semi-Passive Tags Powered by PV Cells.
abstract: This paper presents a developed UHF-RFID tag (865–868 MHz) capable of operating in both passive and semi-passive modes. In semi-passive mode, where the tag is externally powered, the tag significantly extends its read range because of its improved sensitivity. Here, the power was provided by a photovoltaic (PV) cell, instead of the usual approach of using a battery. At an EIRP of 35 dBm, the read ranges were measured as 12.7 m and 15.0 m for vertical and horizontal polarization, respectively, representing remarkable increases of 139% and 168% compared to the passive mode. The PV cell provided enough power, even indoors at low illuminance conditions.

title: Beyond Scores: Earables as Active Recovery Boosters for Longevity and Performance.
abstract: We live in a day and age where longevity and performance are the greatest aspirations of today's society. Endurance athletes are on a quest to minimize their cardiovascular age and boosting their peak performance. Yet, the key to their ambitions lies in their recovery. Current wearables such as Oura Ring, Whoop, UltraHuman, and Garmin (Body Battery) aim at quantifying recovery by means of scores but remain passive—they monitor and occasionally advise, without intervening. With this work, we envision that earables are in the unique situation where they have all the attributes that it takes to move beyond passive tracking to active recovery interventions. By leveraging continuous vital signs and biometrics sensing, acoustic modulation, dynamic noise masking, and even calorie intake detection, earables could help users actively improve sleep, boost their nutrition and fueling, and autonomic balance. We outline this vision, discuss challenges, and call on the community to explore this paradigm shift.

title: EarComp 2025: Sixth International Workshop on Earable Computing.
abstract: The objective of the 6th ACM International Workshop on Earable Computing (EarComp 2025) is to provide an academic forum and bring together researchers, practitioners, and design experts to discuss how sensory earables technologies have and can complement human sensing research. It also aims to provide a launchpad for bold and visionary ideas and serve as a catalyst for advancements in this emerging new Earable Computing research space.

title: Mens Nova in Mundo Virtuali: Immersive Virtual Reality Experiences for Cognitive and Creative Enhancement.
abstract: The workshop ''Mens Nova in Mundo Virtuali: Immersive Virtual Reality Experiences for Cognitive and Creative Enhancement'' explores the transformative potential of immersive virtual reality (VR) technologies in enhancing human cognition and creativity. By leveraging advancements in VR, brain-computer interfaces, and sensory augmentation, this workshop examines how these tools can foster neuroplasticity, improve cognitive functions, and revolutionize creative practices across disciplines. Participants will engage in discussions on topics such as adaptive VR interventions, innovative interaction paradigms, and ethical considerations in cognitive enhancement. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, the workshop aims to establish a roadmap for future research and practical applications, driving the integration of VR into everyday cognitive and creative processes.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Toward High Spatial Resolution and Low Ambiguity in Wideband Signal Receiver Beamforming for VR/AR.
abstract: Accurate angle of arrival (AoA) estimation is critical for virtual and augmented reality applications, as it enhances auditory cues and enables immersive sound-based interactions. However, traditional receiver beamforming methods for AoA estimation using fixed microphone arrays struggle to achieve both high spatial resolution and low ambiguity, especially across wide frequency ranges. In this paper, we propose a novel receiver beamforming system that employs a dynamically reconfigurable circular microphone array with an adjustable radius, paired with a frequency-adaptive ambiguity suppression algorithm. This flexible design allows our system to maintain high spatial resolution, suppress ambiguity lobes effectively, and deliver consistent accuracy across a wide frequency range. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our system surpasses traditional approaches, delivering superior accuracy, robustness, and adaptability in complex acoustic environments.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Assessing Knit Parameters and Performance of Strain Sensors Made from Stainless Steel and Polypyrrole-based Yarns.
abstract: Knitted strain sensors have emerged as a comfortable and user-preferred solution for wearable motion tracking. While knits made from silver-coated yarns are commonly used due to their high conductivity, their susceptibility to degradation in sweat and environmental concerns limit their practicality. This study investigates two alternatives: stainless steel-blend and metal-free polymer-coated yarns, specifically polypyrrole (PPy) on Tencel. We evaluate optimal knit parameters and compare the performance of sensors made from each material. Findings suggest that a dense stitch with at least 30 rows and wale-oriented stress improves sensor performance. The polypyrrole-coated yarn demonstrated superior signal stability and linearity, indicating its promise as an environmentally favourable and reliable material for future wearable strain sensors.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Towards Capturing the Therapeutic Effects of Music in Everyday Life: Building the Beats Dataset.
abstract: Personalised music therapy shows promise as a safe, cost-effective and non-intrusive alternative to pharmacological interventions to support health and wellbeing. However, artificial lab settings limit replication in real-life scenarios and obscure which musical features consistently elicit specific physiological responses. To study how music influences physiological responses (e.g., heart rate) in real environments, we present a framework that leverages commercially available music streaming and wearable sensing technologies to enable continuous, in-the-wild physiological data collection and real-time music tracking. As part of the study design, therapeutically targeted music was systematically selected and listened to in real-world contexts over a sustained experimental period. The proposed system monitors and aligns music listening activity with physiological data and self-reported effects, as well as capturing listeners' demographic information, individual traits, and pre-/post-experiment wellbeing measures. We detailed our stimuli selection process, followed by an overview of the system components. Crucially, this research lays the groundwork for generating a first-of-its-kind dataset to study how music truly influences our physiology in everyday life, offering insights that could guide the development of more effective personalised music-based interventions.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: UbiComp4VRU: Ubiquitous Computing for Vulnerable Road Users.
abstract: Achieving sustainable urban transportation requires not only urban planning but also technological innovation, particularly for vulnerable road users (VRUs) such as cyclists, pedestrians, and e-scooter riders. While active mobility (i.e., cycling and walking) offers environmental and health benefits, VRUs face a higher risk of serious and fatal accidents than vehicles. This full-day workshop will examine how ubiquitous computing, sensing, and communication technologies can improve VRU safety, promote active mobility, and support the development of a sustainable and resilient transportation system while addressing socio-technical aspects such as legal, ethical, psychological, and normative considerations. Therefore, we will invite two keynote speakers, one from technical and one from socio-technical science, and prepare an open discussion session to foster interdisciplinary exchange. The discussion will encourage participants to explore technical innovations and socio-technical implications for enhancing VRU safety and promoting sustainable mobility.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: AudioBuddy: Demonstrating a Wearable and Mobile System Approach for Noise Sensitivity Awareness.
abstract: This demo proposes a novel and practical application called AudioBuddy that uses sensing and tracking technology to facilitate awareness of physiological, psychological, and environmental indicators of potential noise sensitivity experiences. Existing research on noise sensitivity has proposed various approaches for supporting people's experiences, ranging from desensitization therapies to technological systems. However, there is a lack of systems that identify and track characteristics that may indicate the onset of noise sensitivity experiences so that people with noise sensitivity can take preventative actions before reaching stressed states and needing to self-regulate. AudioBuddy is a multi-device application that addresses this aim by leveraging the sensing capabilities of smartwatches for health monitoring, facilitating awareness and information sharing for community support, and presenting users with strategies for managing and regulating noise sensitivity experiences.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: An Interactive Activities of Daily Living Training System with Color-Based Motion Tracking for Early Stage Patients with Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Currently, research on Activities of Daily Living (ADL) training for patients with Alzheimer's Disease (AD) remains scarce, with existing approaches focusing primarily on pharmacological treatment or general rehabilitation, lacking comprehensive tools to address cognitive and motor degeneration. In addition, patients' ability to perform ADL is highly dependent on caregivers for urgent assistance, exacerbated caregiver time, and psychological burdens, while not providing sustained improvement for patients. This study introduces an ADL training system tailored for early- to mid-stage AD patients, aimed at mitigating cognitive decline and improving the autonomy and sense of achievement of patients. The system integrates physical interaction products with a user interface platform, employing Python and OpenCV for precise tracking of the motion trajectory to assess movement execution. Furthermore, an animation module developed in Unity provides real-time feedback and dynamic guidance, optimizing the learning experience. By integrating innovative technologies, the system offers a scientifically grounded and systematic approach to training in ADL, thus supporting cognitive maintenance and improving the quality of life for patients with AD.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: GrowChat: Promoting Remote Informal Communication through Character Creation and Development for Team Well-Being.
abstract: Informal communication enhances not only team productivity and creativity but also the well-being of team members. However, remote environments greatly reduce such opportunities. To address this, we propose GrowChat, a prototype system that utilizes team-based character creation and development to promote remote informal communication (RIC). GrowChat encourages each team member to participate in RIC by providing a mechanism through which members jointly create a character, and the character evolves based on the amount of communication. We compared two conditions: one involving only character development, and another combining both creation and development, examining their effects on RIC and psychological factors. Results showed that character creation lowered psychological barriers to communication, while development encouraged sustained interaction. The combination enhanced attachment to the character and strengthened team unity.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Immersive Bridge Inspection: Quantifying the Benefits of XR for Anomaly Detection.
abstract: We present an immersive bridge inspection tool as part of a digital twin for bridges that merges virtual reality (VR) with AI-assisted anomaly detection to evaluate how extended reality (XR) tools can modernize bridge inspections. Two tasks were studied: (i) relocating previously reported anomalies and (ii) detecting new surface anomalies using XR technologies. XR cues and simulated AI prompts were compared with manual inspection for five key performance indicators. Results show that XR + AI cut average detection time by 51%, boosted accuracy by 38%, lowered subjectivity by 11%, and reduced cognitive workload by 23 NASA-TLX points. A post-study survey yielded favorable usability and usefulness ratings, although some volunteers experienced VR-induced discomfort. These findings demonstrate the promise of XR and AI to accelerate, objectify, and lighten the mental load of structural assessments, while highlighting usability challenges that must be addressed for field deployment.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Integrated Radar Sensing and Communications: convergence, co-design and learning.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems operate within shared, congested, or even contested spectrum, aiming to deliver high performance in both wireless communications and radio frequency (RF) sensing. Communications and sensing functionalities are co-designed for mutual benefit. ISAC systems share hardware and antenna resources, use joint waveforms, and function within shared spectra and exchange awareness about their radio environments to jointly optimize performance. ISAC technology has opened genuinely new lines of research and development in emerging 6G systems rather than merely being an evolution of 5G. ISAC takes advantage of the ongoing parallel convergence of modern radar and multi-antenna communications technologies. Sensing may be a service, can aid communications, and conversely, communications may aid sensing. ISAC is expected to provide unprecedented quality of experience towards reliable, resilient, and ubiquitous connectivity, beyond the high data-rate transmission of bits. This talk focuses on various waveform design, signal processing, optimization, adaptation and reinforcement learning techniques employed to achieve desired sensing and communications performances in multicarrier (MC) and multiantenna ISAC systems. Examples on waveform design, optimization, resource allocation in multi-user and multi target scenarios are provided.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Prototype Context-Aware On-Skin Interfaces for Socially Adaptive Biofeedback.
abstract: Ubiquitous computing opens new possibilities for communicating physiological states through on-skin interfaces, supporting emotional awareness, empathy, and well-being. However, research efforts remain largely exclusive due to barriers in prototyping and a lack of interdisciplinary engagement. In this work, I argue that exploring socially expressive on-skin interaction requires platforms that make prototyping accessible across disciplines. I introduced SkinKit, the first on-skin prototyping toolkit that lowers the entry barrier for making. I developed SkinLink, a fabrication approach that supports on-body adjustments to optimize prototype iteration. I demonstrate ECSkin, an adaptive on-skin display technology of modular electrochromic films, to expand the display modalities. These platforms pave the way for empowering co-design collaborations with multidisciplinary practitioners. To carry forward the explorations, I initiate the research to engage psychology, communication, and design experts to identify design opportunities and considerations for social biofeedback and on-skin interactions. Finally, I describe how achieving context-aware on-skin biofeedback systems can be essential for tailoring feedback to social cues, communication intent, and user-defined preferences. Through this research agenda, I aim to advance a vision of ubiquitous computing that supports interdisciplinary exploration and broadens the context-responsive applications of on-skin interfaces across real-world settings.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: UltrasonicSpheres: Localized, Multi-Channel Sound Spheres Using Off-the-Shelf Speakers and Earables.
abstract: We present a demo of UltrasonicSpheres, a novel system for location-specific audio delivery using wearable earphones that decode ultrasonic signals into audible sound. Unlike conventional beamforming setups, UltrasonicSpheres relies on single ultrasonic speakers to broadcast localized audio with multiple channels, each encoded on a distinct ultrasonic carrier frequency. Users wearing our acoustically transparent earphones can demodulate their selected stream, such as exhibit narrations in a chosen language, while remaining fully aware of ambient environmental sounds. The experience preserves spatial audio perception, giving the impression that the sound originates directly from the physical location of the source. This enables personalized, localized audio without requiring pairing, tracking, or additional infrastructure. Importantly, visitors not equipped with the earphones are unaffected, as the ultrasonic signals are inaudible to the human ear. Our demo invites participants to explore multiple audio zones and experience how UltrasonicSpheres supports unobtrusive delivery of personalized sound in public spaces.

title: Ubiquitous Well-being: Patchable AI Unites Computing and Psychological Science.
abstract: Brief psychological interventions (e.g., values affirmation) improve health and learning, yet an infrastructure for personalized, scalable, and timely delivery is missing. We propose that ubiquitous computing can transform static interventions into evolving services. This work introduces Patchable AI, a framework in which chatbots become continuously learning systems through hot-swappable, auditable ''intervention patches'' guarded by safety policies. Four architectural layers—sensor triggers, policy guardrails, patch registry, and conversation broker—allow evolution without retraining underlying models. To provide materials for brief psychological interventions, we conducted a large-scale data collection effort using a custom web-scriber to capture nearly all publicly available psychological and journaling prompts (N = 54,251) from 2015 onward, yielding short, crisp contents structured for patchable deployment. Our values-affirmation case study demonstrates how Patchable AI aligns psychological theory, organizational policy, and technical affordances, offering a roadmap for scalable, personalized well-being services. This research aims to (1) apply a ubiquitous-computing framework across disciplines—education, public health, workplace training—and (2) advance intervention science by embedding human-centered AI that turns static protocols into adaptive, context-aware services. We also outline broader implications, showing how Patchable AI can underpin living support systems across domains.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: LoRadar: Capturing and Detecting Satellite-Ground LoRa Signals in the Wild.
abstract: LoRa has emerged as a promising technology for satellite-based IoT due to its low power, long-range capabilities, and resilience to interference. However, empirical research on satellite-ground LoRa communication remains limited due to the lack of accessible physical-layer data. In this work, we present the first large-scale IQ dataset collected from real-world satellite-ground LoRa links using commercial terminals and on-orbit satellites operating in the 399–403 MHz band. To extract valid signals from noisy, low-SNR environments with unknown configurations, we develop a non-cooperative LoRa signal detection system, LoRadar, combining blind parameter estimation and sweep-based frequency-domain correlation. Evaluations show LoRadar effectively identifies multiple PHY configurations and accurately detects preambles on real satellite data. LoRadar provides a reproducible foundation for future research in satellite IoT signal analysis, protocol design, and system benchmarking.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Revisiting Multi-Agent GAN for Multimodal Time Series Generation in Human Sensing and mHealth Applications.
abstract: The development of reliable Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions for human sensing and mobile health (mHealth) increasingly depends on large, diverse, and multimodal time series (TS) datasets. However, real-world data collection faces significant challenges, resulting in data scarcity that hinders progress. Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) have emerged as a promising tool for synthetic TS generation, yet their application to multimodal physiological and behavioral signals remains problematic. In this work, we critically evaluate leading multi-agent GAN models proposed for multimodal TS generation, using two real-world datasets targeting stress detection and human activity recognition (HAR) tasks. Our findings reveal consistent and substantial performance drops in Train-on-Synthetic, Test-on-Real (TSTR) settings across all models and datasets. Data augmentation also yields marginal improvements in a few instances, and a light degradation in most cases. These outcomes reflect the poor usability of synthetic data, especially for complex tasks like multi-class HAR, due to weak cross-modal generation. Further intrinsic quality assessment confirms notable discrepancies between real and synthetic distributions across sensing modalities. To address these issues, we propose a novel GAN framework combining TS-centric multi-task learning with state-of-the-art Transformer architectures for multivariate TS forecasting, aimed at advancing multimodal synthesis for downstream human sensing applications.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Evaluating Rhythmic Representations in Mental Health from Wearable Devices Using the GLOBEM Datasets.
abstract: Recent studies have linked depression to biobehavioral rhythms, which are repeating cycles of physiological, psychological, social, and environmental patterns captured by wearable devices. However, their predictive potential still needs further exploration. This paper investigates whether modeling periodic patterns in longitudinal data, using cosine transformations and mathematical rhythm modeling, can help machine learning (ML) models learn hidden periodic patterns and improve the interpretability of depression prediction methods. Using the GLOBEM datasets, we extracted statistical, rhythmic, and data-driven learned features from wearable and mobile phone data. We observed that periodic features like SSA and Cosinor improve depression detection, with Transformer and Reordering models showing the most benefit from SSA, while statistical features often lead to better balanced accuracy. Lastly, we observed that features aimed at guiding models to learn hidden periodical patterns, such as the cosine of day and week, improve performance in models like Transformer. Feature importance analysis shows that statistical and periodic features, especially sleep and screen duration times or their corresponding phase and trend, consistently rank as the most influential across most iterations with different feature sets.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Evaluating the Quality of Counterfactual Explanations in Multivariate Time-Series.
abstract: Counterfactual explanations (CFEs) offer a promising approach for understanding personalized psychological processes captured through Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA). In particular, generating CFEs for time points associated with mental health deterioration can help identify alternative changes that might prevent such outcomes. To assess the quality of generated CFEs on time-series data, we propose a 3-level framework: per explanation (based on feature changes, proximity, and model confidence), per time point (based on structure and diversity through clustering), and per individual temporal dynamics. Applying this framework to a real-world time-series EMA dataset, we demonstrate how we assess the validity and interpretability of large volumes of CFEs.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Preliminary Evaluation of Piezoelectric Thin Film Sensors for Arterial and Venous Pulse Detection Using an Epidermal Neck Patch.
abstract: Wearable technology for monitoring blood pulse waveforms in the cervical area is still in a developmental stage, primarily due to challenges in accurate sensor placement and proper signal detection on the neck. In this study, two commercial piezoelectric thin film sensors were compared to identify the most suitable one for integration into a biocompatible epidermal neck patch. Of the two, the one with the largest sensitive area was chosen to carry out measurements on a healthy male subject in two different body positions: supine and sitting. The ECG signal was also acquired as a temporal reference to distinguish physiological blood pulse waveforms from those containing artifacts. Signal processing techniques applied to recorded signals have demonstrated the ability of the piezoelectric thin film sensor to clearly distinguish between arterial and venous blood pulses. Moreover, thanks to the used non-disposable adhesive patch, these preliminary results pave the way for telemedicine applications focused on head and neck vascular health, enabling the screening of population and contributing to personalized healthcare and overall public wellbeing.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: A Social Compass: Guiding Self-Regulation in High-Arousal Moments with Ubiquitous Sensing.
abstract: Social interactions often trigger physiological stress responses that can impair communication effectiveness and well-being. This paper presents SocialCompass, a proof-of-concept framework that leverages the large multimodal foundation model, ImageBind, to detect high-stress social moments and provide timely self-regulation support. Unlike existing emotion recognition systems that focus on classification accuracy, SocialCompass prioritizes real-world deployment and user autonomy. Our core innovation lies in a novel zero-shot inference strategy that bridges multiple public datasets without requiring direct cross-dataset alignment. We train a social context classifier on high-frequency Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) and audio features from the ExtraSensory dataset, while developing an arousal inference model that uses ImageBind's cross-modal semantic alignment to compare real-time sensor embeddings with conceptual text anchors derived from psychological concepts. This dual-model approach allows us to identify High-Arousal Social Events (HASE) in real-world settings. We propose a three-phase implementation strategy culminating in a demonstration on smart glasses. Initial feasibility analysis shows promising potential for real-world deployment while highlighting key technical and ethical considerations for socially-aware computing systems.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: ReflectAI: Promoting Student Wellbeing using LLM-Driven Multimodal Sensing System for Proactive Behavioral Feedback.
abstract: University students today face a growing mental health crisis, yet existing wellbeing technologies often operate in isolation, rely heavily on manual self-tracking, and struggle to detect subtle behavioral changes or provide timely, personalized support. To address these limitations, we present ReflectAI, a proactive digital companion that combines multimodal passive sensing with large language model (LLM) reasoning to deliver context-aware, empathetic wellbeing feedback by integrating two key components: a contextual recognizer that semantically interprets behavioral cues from sensor and schedule data, and an LLM-based reasoning engine that infers user intent and generates psychologically informed responses. Leveraging few-shot prompting and pretrained psychological knowledge, the system interprets behavioral summaries—such as reduced mobility or irregular sleep—and delivers timely, adaptive feedback without requiring manual input or rule-based classifiers. Preliminary evaluation on StudentLife and GLOBEM datasets demonstrate promising output quality, validating the feasibility of LLM-powered behavior-aware feedback generation.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Estimating Transfer Costs from Real Human Mobility Data in Urban Transit.
abstract: This study proposes a method to quantitatively estimate transfer costs in urban public transportation using large-scale IC card data from Japan's Kansai region. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on surveys, our model empirically infers transfer penalties from observed mobility. We extend the cost-based radiation model developed for inter-city travel to intra-city contexts by incorporating station-level land use. Transfer costs are estimated by calibrating the travel cost function to maximize the Common Part of Commuters (CPC), a commonly used metric for comparing predicted and observed flows. Our findings indicate that the optimal uniform transfer cost corresponds to approximately 30 minutes of generalized travel time. Furthermore, disaggregated analysis reveals significant variation in transfer costs depending on physical and institutional factors, with the highest burdens arising from inter-station, inter-operator transfers. These results provide insights for designing more effective transfer policies.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Listening to the Mind: Earable Acoustic Sensing of Cognitive Load.
abstract: Earable acoustic sensing offers a powerful and non-invasive modality for capturing fine-grained auditory and physiological signals directly from the ear canal, enabling continuous and context-aware monitoring of cognitive states. As earable devices become increasingly embedded in daily life, they provide a unique opportunity to sense mental effort and perceptual load in real time through auditory interactions. In this study, we present the first investigation of cognitive load inference through auditory perception using acoustic signals captured by off-the-shelf in-ear devices. We designed speech-based listening tasks to induce varying levels of cognitive load, while concurrently embedding acoustic stimuli to evoke Stimulus Frequency Otoacoustic Emission (SFOAEs) as a proxy for cochlear responsiveness. Statistical analysis revealed a significant association (p < 0.01) between increased cognitive load and changes in auditory sensitivity, with 63.2% of participants showing peak sensitivity at 3 kHz. Notably, sensitivity patterns also varied across demographic subgroups, suggesting opportunities for personalized sensing. Our findings demonstrate that earable acoustic sensing can support scalable, real-time cognitive load monitoring in natural settings, laying a foundation for future applications in augmented cognition, where everyday auditory technologies adapt to and support the users mental health.

title: Behavioral Indicators of Loneliness: Predicting University Students' Loneliness Scores from Smartphone Sensing Data.
abstract: Loneliness is a critical mental health issue among university students, yet traditional monitoring methods rely primarily on retrospective self-reports and often lack real-time behavioral context. This study explores the use of passive smartphone sensing data to predict loneliness levels, addressing the limitations of existing approaches in capturing its dynamic nature. We integrate smartphone sensing with machine learning and large language models respectively to develop generalized and personalized models. Our Random Forest generalized models achieved mean absolute errors of 3.29 at midterm and 3.98 (out of 32) at the end of semester on the UCLA Loneliness Scale (short form), identifying smartphone screen usage and location mobility to be key predictors. The one-shot approach leveraging large language models reduced prediction errors by up to 42% compared to zero-shot inference. The one-shot results from personalized models highlighted screen usage, application usage, battery, and location transitions as salient behavioral indicators. These findings demonstrate the potential of smartphone sensing data for scalable and interpretable loneliness detection in digital mental health.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: A Convolutional Block Attention Module and Multi-band Fusion Network for Embedded AR-SSVEP BCI Systems.
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCI) based on augmented reality steady-state visual evoked potentials (AR-SSVEP) face critical challenges in mobile environments, including low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) from dry electrodes and limited computational resources on mobile embedded platforms. To optimize the AR-SSVEP system performance, this study comprehensively considers the stimulus-response coupling mechanism integrating visual optical principles with deep learning-based classification. First, we designed an optimal AR visual stimulation configuration scheme capable of adaptively adjusting key parameters. Second, to address the time-varying non-stationary characteristics of SSVEP and inter-electrode quality variations in dry electrode systems, we propose CBAM-FNet-a lightweight SSVEP detection algorithm that incorporates the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) with multi-band fusion. The algorithm achieves classification accuracies of 93.84% on benchmark datasets and 74.43% on our self-collected AR-SSVEP dataset, representing performance improvements of up to 22.96% over state-of-the-art methods. Real-time implementation on an embedded unmanned vehicle platform demonstrates 65% control accuracy with an information transfer rate of 50.35 bits/min, validating the practical value of CBAM-FNet in embedded BCI applications and overcoming hardware-imposed performance limitations.
conference_title: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing

title: Can Large Language Models Identify Materials from Radar Signals?
abstract: Accurately identifying the material composition of objects is a critical capability for AI robots powered by large language models (LLMs) to perform context-aware manipulation. Radar technologies offer a promising sensing modality for material recognition task. When combined with deep learning, radar technologies have demonstrated strong potential in identifying the material of various objects. However, existing radar-based solutions are often constrained to closed-set object categories and typically require task-specific data collection to train deep learning models, largely limiting their practical applicability. This raises an important question: Can we leverage the powerful reasoning capabilities of pre-trained LLMs to directly infer material composition from raw radar signals? Answering this question is non-trivial due to the inherent redundancy of radar signals and the fact that pre-trained LLMs have no prior exposure to raw radar data during training. To address this, we introduce LLMaterial, the first study to investigate the feasibility of using LLM to identify materials directly from radar signals. First, we introduce a physics-informed signal processing pipeline that distills high-redundancy radar raw data into a set of compact intermediate parameters that encapsulate the material's intrinsic characteristics. Second, we adopt a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) strategy to provide the LLM with domain-specific knowledge, enabling it to interpret and reason over the extracted intermediate parameters. Leveraging this integration, the LLM is empowered to perform step-by-step reasoning on the condensed radar features, achieving open-set material recognition directly from raw radar signals. Preliminary results show that LLMaterial can effectively distinguish among a variety of common materials, highlighting its strong potential for real-world material identification applications.

title: AISE: Adaptive Importance Sampling Events for Low Power Eye Tracking.
abstract: Eye tracking technology decodes human visual cognition by analyzing eye movements and is widely used in psychology, human-computer interaction, and clinical diagnosis. Traditional frame based cameras suffer from high redundant data, motion blur, and limited dynamic range, making it difficult to meet the low-power real-time processing requirements of wearable devices. This study proposes a low-power eye tracking framework based on event cameras, achieving three innovations: 1) Design an eye module mask identification algorithm based on event flow; 2) Design an events importance sampling algorithm and filtering mechanism based on the local SNN hardware platform; 3) Implement end-to-end SNN networks with theoretical chip performance as low as less than 5mW. This technology provides a high-performance and highly robust next-generation eye-tracking solution for AR/VR devices and neuroscience research.
